n: Oil and Commodity Price-Cap and Ship-to-Ship Evasion
ds: Where price caps or embargoes apply to oil and other commodities, attempts to circumvent them may involve inflated or opaque attestations, intermediary traders, undisclosed ship-to-ship transfers and ageing or unusual tankers. Detection draws on trade documents, pricing, vessel data and the quality of attestations from counterparties.

rat: Commodity traders, attestations, tanker insurance and ship-to-ship transfers.

ind.n: Attestations of price compliance without supporting invoices
ind.cx: Counterparties provide generic declarations but cannot supply itemised contracts and invoices showing the price of oil and services.
ind.ds: Counterparties provide generic declarations but cannot supply itemised contracts and invoices showing the price of oil and services.

ind.n: Cargo priced near cap with inflated freight, insurance or ancillary charges
ind.cx: Separately invoiced services carry unusually high costs.
ind.fp: Market volatility and war-risk premiums raise costs.
ind.ds: Separately invoiced services carry unusually high costs.

ind.n: Tanker with older age, unusual classification, or no recognised P&I
ind.cx: Vessels outside mainstream commercial insurance and class regimes carry the cargo.
ind.ds: Vessels outside mainstream commercial insurance and class regimes carry the cargo.

ind.n: Ship-to-ship transfers with no clear commercial purpose
ind.cx: Cargo transferred at sea off the route and followed by a different declared destination.
ind.fp: STS is normal in oil trade.
ind.ds: Vessel meets others at sea off normal transfer areas, followed by a changed declared destination.
ind.cn: Ship-to-ship transfers without clear commercial purpose

ind.n: Newly established trading intermediaries in hub jurisdictions
ind.cx: Recently incorporated traders with little track record buying and reselling restricted-origin cargo.
ind.fp: New traders enter the market regularly.
ind.ds: A recently formed customer with little history or track record quickly records large turnover or trades in high-value or restricted goods.
ind.cn: Newly established customer with rapid high-value activity

ind.n: Payments in alternative currencies or via smaller banks
ind.cx: Payments denominated or routed to avoid mainstream channels.
ind.ds: Payments denominated or routed to avoid mainstream channels.

ind.n: Discrepancy between loading port, origin documents and tracking
ind.cx: Declared origin differs from vessel tracking and port records.
ind.fp: Port calls vary with operational changes.
ind.ds: Declared origin differs from vessel tracking and port records.

ind.n: Repeated changes of buyer or consignee mid-voyage
ind.cx: Cargo ownership shifts while at sea without clear commercial reason.
ind.ds: Shipments or cargoes are re-routed, re-invoiced or have ownership shifted through successive parties without clear commercial reason.
ind.cn: Repeated change of consignee or buyer in transit

ctl.ds: Compares declared unit prices, award values, fees and ancillary costs with reference databases, estimates and comparable contracts, and requires documented rationale for outliers. It detects over- and under-invoicing and inflated awards.

Maintains records of identification, transactions, decisions and exceptions for the required period, with logs of deviations and a retrievable audit trail. It allows regulators and investigators to reconstruct events and supports later challenge of decisions.

ctl.n: Sampling, quality assurance and analytics audit
ctl.ds: Takes periodic samples of customer files, alert decisions, relied-upon files or analytical datasets and tests them for exceptions, duplicates and errors, feeding findings back to owners and training. It independently confirms that controls work as designed.

Confirms the existence of underlying goods, services or receivables directly with the obligor or through inspection before funds are advanced. It defeats fictitious invoices and transactions that exist only on paper.

ctl.n: Trade document review and consistency checking
ctl.ds: Trained staff and automated checks review goods, parties, routes, descriptions and codes across invoice, bill of lading and payment documents. It exposes mismatches and falsified paper.

ctl.n: Vessel due diligence and tracking analytics
ctl.ds: Verifies vessel identity, ownership, flag history, insurance and class, and analyses tracking data for gaps, loitering, ship-to-ship transfers and spoofing. It addresses sanctions and illicit-trade evasion at sea.

Requires documentary evidence of origin, legal sourcing, custody and conformity with responsible-sourcing standards, including for informal or recycled supply. It keeps illicitly sourced goods from entering the financed or traded chain.

ctl.n: Senior management approval and risk acceptance
ctl.ds: Requires named senior management or a committee to approve onboarding, continuation or waivers for higher-risk relationships, with documented mitigations and periodic re-approval. It adds accountability and an independent challenge to risk acceptance.
Risk-based vetting of intermediaries, brokers, partners and suppliers covering ownership, experience, references, public-official links and selection rationale. It limits exposure through proxies.

ctl.n: Correspondent respondent due diligence and risk rating
ctl.ds: Assesses respondent banks' jurisdiction, ownership, regulation, products and AML controls at onboarding using questionnaires and risk rating, including counterparty bank review. It sets the basis for correspondent relationships.

Alerts on unusual countries, corridors, deposit locations and geolocation dispersion relative to the customer profile or on activity near designated risk regions. It focuses review on geographic anomalies.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.
